# Loophole: the Rat Trap

You are manipulating a physical string puzzle in a physics simulator through the **`loophole` MCP server**
(tools `get_state`, `grab`, `move`, `release`, `give_up`). The simulator's source is not available to you; the score
is computed afterwards by independently replaying your actions. When you are done (or out of ideas), simply stop.

You are manipulating a physical string puzzle ("the Rat Trap") in a physics simulator, through tools.

Coordinates in millimetres: x = left -> right, y = front -> back (the front is -y), z = up. A rectangular wooden FRAME
stands upright in the plane y = 0 on a base plank (top of the base at z = 20). The frame's
opening is 120 mm wide (x from -60 to 60) and 200 mm tall (z from 35 to
235); its rails are 15 mm thick. Inside the opening:
- UPPER POST: a horizontal bar (20 mm square) from the RIGHT rail leftwards, 95 mm long, at z = 168.3.
- LOWER POST: the same from the LEFT rail rightwards, at z = 101.7.
- LEFT DOWEL: a thin vertical rod (radius 3 mm) at x = -20 hanging from the top rail, passing down through
  a hole (radius 6.5 mm) in the upper post, ending in a SPHERE (radius 15 mm) centred at z = 135.
- RIGHT DOWEL: a thin vertical rod at x = 20 rising from the bottom rail, up through a hole in the lower post, ending in a
  vertical RING (major radius 23 mm, tube 4 mm) centred at [20.0, 0.0, 168.3], whose axis runs
  left-right; the upper post passes through the ring.
Named passages (gaps the string can go through): {"post_upper.hole": "centre [-15.3, 0.0, 168.3] mm, passage axis [0, 0, 1]", "post_lower.hole": "centre [24.8, 0.0, 101.7] mm, passage axis [0, 0, 1]", "ring.inside": "centre [20.0, 0.0, 182.8] mm, passage axis [1, 0, 0]", "gap.sphere_upper": "centre [-14.0, 0.0, 154.2] mm, passage axis [0, 1, 0]", "gap.sphere_lower": "centre [-14.0, 0.0, 115.8] mm, passage axis [0, 1, 0]", "gap.upper_left": "centre [-47.5, 0.0, 168.3] mm, passage axis [0, 0, 1]", "gap.lower_right": "centre [47.5, 0.0, 101.7] mm, passage axis [0, 0, 1]"}.

The STRING is a closed loop of length 603 mm, radius 1.2 mm, modelled as 143 nodes (indices 0..142;
node 0 and node 142 are the same point, the loop is closed). A MOUSE (a bead of radius 11 mm) is tied to node 71; it is too big
for the dowel holes, the ring and the gaps beside the sphere, but fits through the gaps at the free ends of the posts.
At the start the loop is wrapped around the right dowel (between the bottom rail and the lower post), both strands
running out over the front of the base into a wide loop in front of the frame.

GOAL: free the string loop (with the mouse) completely from the wooden structure. It counts as solved when the loop,
frozen in its current shape, could slide away to infinity in some straight direction without touching anything.
Checked automatically after every action. Score: solved -> 1 - 0.5 * actions / 852; not solved -> 0.3 x the
fraction of the milestones of a reference solution you reached, in order (0 if none). Pressing the string into the
wood (more than 1 mm) ends the episode with 0.

TOOLS: two grippers (handle 0 and 1). grab(handle, node) takes the string at a node; move(handle, dx, dy, dz) moves
that gripper by up to 30 mm per call (the string follows; the motion stops early if blocked); release(handle).
get_state() shows the string. render() shows images (if available). Budget: 852 grab/move/release actions in total;
get_state / render are free. Plan, then act. The string cannot pass through the wood or through itself.

python3 -c '
import json, urllib.request

def get_state():
    url = "http://loophole-sim:8000/mcp"
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream"}
    data = json.dumps({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "get_state", "arguments": {}}}).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers, method="POST")
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
        body = resp.read().decode()
        for line in body.splitlines():
            if line.startswith("data: "):
                res = json.loads(line[6:])
                return json.loads(res["result"]["content"][0]["text"])

s = get_state()
print("Actions:", s["actions_used"], "Left:", s["actions_left"])
print("Mouse:", s["mouse_node"], s["mouse_mm"])
print("Grippers:", s["grippers"])
print("Keys:", list(s.keys()))
'
